Commoner (scullion) is a dnd5e:monsters:commoner of the faction `kitchen`, standing at q -19, r -9 in Kitchen (region-kitchen), facing ne; it looks like dnd5e:npcs:kingdom:peasant-female-01.

The speaker can say the line “There's a coin in it if you know a way out of here.” (`favour`) to Commoner (scullion). It is said at `speak` (the default): its words reach everyone in the speaker's room (the wall partition the speaker stands in), and anyone in the next room within 30 feet of the speaker by the way through an open doorway (a closed door stops them), and whoever it is said to, wherever they stand. Whoever sees the speaker is told who said it; whoever the words reach and does not see the speaker hears the words — and which line it was, the roll, whether it worked and what it taught — from someone unnamed; whoever only sees it said learns neither the words, which line it was, whether it worked, nor what it taught; whoever the words do not reach may still notice a voice by passive Perception, never a whisper; the one it is said to is named only to those who see them. It is a plain line: it rolls nothing, cannot be missed, and costs nothing on either clock.

When the line “There's a coin in it if you know a way out of here.” (`favour`) is said, Commoner (scullion) answers “The grate by the hearth. Lift it. One way climbs to the chapel, the other drops to the cells.”, at `speak`: its words reach everyone in Commoner (scullion)'s room (the wall partition Commoner (scullion) stands in), and anyone in the next room within 30 feet of Commoner (scullion) by the way through an open doorway (a closed door stops them), and whoever it is said to, wherever they stand and whoever sees Commoner (scullion) answer and caught none of the line is told only that Commoner (scullion) answered and what Commoner (scullion) is seen doing, and, if they see the speaker, sees the line said without its words.
